completenessChecks: All 25 narrative and answer paragraphs, 9 bold prompts and 4 section headings present in original order.

voiceChecks: Opening anecdote about the spaghetti photo kept with its deadpan 'the lady earned a reprimand and a two-week suspension'.
Nim's narrated concession ('And honestly, she deserves it') kept at the same weight.
'fixing me with melting eyes' kept as the one flirtatious narrative touch.

decisions: Headline 'מגילת אסתר' rendered 'The Scroll of Esther', keeping the pun on the biblical book and her first name; the spelling 'Ester Rada' follows the inventory and her established stage name.
'ברוך הגבר' rendered 'Blessed is the man', the phrase's literal sense, since the pun on Baruch Goldstein's name does not survive in English; noted as a loss.
'הלהקה' rendered 'The Troupe', the usual English title of the Israeli film and musical.
'דאוס' kept as 'Deus'; '7 לילות' as '7 Nights'; 'ערוץ הילדים' as 'the Children's Channel'.
'אמנוצ'י' rendered 'arty-nude'; 'הפאסון' as 'the front'; 'הארד קור' as 'hardcore'; 'ג'יפה' as 'filth'; 'חתיכת וולקאם' as 'some welcome'.
'אולפנה', 'moshavim' and 'ulpana' kept as Hebrew terms without glosses, matching the original's assumed reader.
Quotations are translations of the published Hebrew, not reconstructed English speech.
sourceProblems: Source record: online version is complete, but the publisher promoted further material in the print Pnai Plus issue; print-only material is not included or reconstructed.
Source has an unmatched quotation mark at the end of 'קפצו שתי כיתות'"'; normalized in English without changing wording.
